idiom_name: Array/ContiguousArray of struct values, with withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer for manual columnar layouts
implementation_notes: Swift's structs are value types stored inline, so an array of structs is already the packed layout the pattern asks for: records carry no object header and no per-element allocation, and iteration touches contiguous storage with no ARC traffic. ContiguousArray makes the guarantee explicit - it 'always stores its elements in a contiguous region of memory', whereas Array may bridge to NSArray when Element is a class or @objc protocol - so struct elements plus ContiguousArray are the safe default. What replaces the classic structure: values in one array addressed by Int indices (or a struct-of-arrays with one array per field), with withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer/UnsafeMutableRawPointer for hand-controlled layouts or C/Accelerate interop inside the closure. Generic algorithms and lazy sequences are the ordinary style, but kernels should stay counted loops over arrays.
pitfalls: The buffer pointer from withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer must not escape the closure: growing or replacing the array afterwards invalidates it, and exclusivity checks make escaping views undefined.
Array's storage may be bridged to NSArray when Element is a class or @objc protocol, which loses the contiguity guarantee - use ContiguousArray (or struct elements) for hot data.
Copy-on-write copies a large array whenever a second reference exists; a shared 'view' parameter can silently double memory, so pass buffers or use uniquely-referenced storage for big pools.
Float and Double do not mix implicitly: a mixed-precision record pads and converts, so keep one width per column.
